subject: Life Skills
title: Email Etiquette That Works
description: A micro-lesson that makes Email Etiquette That Works usable.

hook.text: The average office worker receives 121 emails per day. Most are skimmed in under five seconds.

buildup.text: A vague subject line means your email gets buried. Clear subjects drive faster responses.

discovery.text: Put the action item in the first sentence. Backstory belongs below, not before the point.

twist.text: Reply-all is the most feared button in offices. One misfire can reach hundreds of inboxes instantly.

climax.text: Keep emails under five sentences. If it takes more, schedule a call or meeting instead.

punchline.text: Respect their inbox and they'll respect yours.

quiz.question: Where should you place the action item in an email?
options: At the very end for emphasis
In the first sentence for clarity
